## 分诊 · `domain:services` / `priority:p2` / `pm:queue`

**Anchor read, not guessed.** The test is `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/durability-swallow-repair.test.ts` (718 lines, present on `origin/main` `f1d7872`, 2026-09-05T00:30:54Z) ⇒ `domain:services`.

⚠️ ⭐ **Name collision to guard against**: there is a **second** file called `durability-swallow-repair.test.ts` — `packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-service-plugin.durability-swallow-repair.test.ts`. ⛔ Do not grep by basename; this card is the plugin-auth one.

### Grade — p2

⭐ **Three PR-CI reds in one hour, on three PRs whose diffs do not touch plugin-auth or anything it imports at test time** (#15554 `.objectui-sha` bump, #15562 and #15571 both `packages/lint`) — same test, same line, same 10 000 ms timeout. And the attribution is properly controlled from both sides:

- **merge-group runs of the same shard passed** between 21:15Z and 22:36Z (#15559, #15532, #15570) ⇒ ⛔ **not red on main**;
- `check-test-completeness` on the red runs reports every other package accounted for;
- ⭐ the smoking gun is on the run itself: **`import 482.93s`** against a **10 s** test budget ⇒ the shard's runner was heavily loaded. The test is red **under PR-CI shard load**, not on its own merits.

⇒ Same tax as its sibling **#15545**: a timing failure in a package the red PRs do not touch, costing three authors a diagnosis and two legitimate re-runs. Not p1 (nothing ships wrong; the assertion's subject is sound). Not p3 (three reds in one hour is a rate, not an anecdote).

### Boundary test — Tests only, no manual floor

### ⛔ The fence — identical to #15545's and equally absolute

> ⛔ **Not to skip, quarantine or widen the timeout blindly.** The test pins **#12981 batch 6**'s swallow repair (a run-level audit row must be **REPORTED**, never vanish); **it needs to stay a real assertion.**

Adopted and binding. ⚠️ **"Widen the timeout" is the tempting non-fix here** and it is explicitly excluded *blindly* — a larger budget with no measurement just moves the threshold until the next loaded runner.

⇒ **What a fix owes**: a measurement of **what the test waits on for 10 s** — a timer? a real engine boot per case? the audit sink? — and then either **a faster fixture** or **a budget that matches the measured cost, with the reason written at the test.** ⭐ The written reason is the part that stops this recurring: a bare number returns as a mystery, a number with its measurement attached can be re-checked.

### ⭐ Read with #15545 — two instances, one shape, and possibly one answer

Both are **timing failures under PR-CI load in packages the red PRs do not touch** (#15545: a `packages/cli` e2e socket race that **evicted PR #15506 from the merge queue**). ⛔ They stay two cards — different packages, different mechanisms (socket readiness vs a fixed budget), different owners. ⚠️ But **two in one day suggests the shard's load profile is the common factor**, and if a third appears the honest card is about the shard, not about a third test. ⇒ Worth one sentence in whichever fix lands second.

### ⭐ Queue hygiene — recorded because it was done correctly

One re-run of the failed jobs per PR on **#15562** and **#15571** (the single legitimate re-run per red the dispatch rules allow), each with a **standing-down note naming this card**. ⛔ **#15554 was NOT re-run** because it carries a **real** red of its own (`check:objectui-pin-citations`, 8 stale anchors — its own rework, and the subject of #15604 routed tonight). ⇒ That is exactly the discipline: a re-run spent only where the failure is established as not-this-PR's, never to paper over a real red sitting beside it.

⛔ Not a claim, not a dispatch — routing only.

## PM routing — this card stays OPEN, and PR #15914 will not close it

PR [#15914](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/15914) fixes the site this card was filed from, and its author proposed closing all three cards that name it (#14998, #15852, this one). **I am striking this card's `Fixes` line.** #14998 and #15852 do close on that merge; this one does not, and the reason is a card the same author filed in the same run.

### The distinction

⚠️ **This card is not about a test — it is about a shard.** Its own observation is *"three unrelated PRs red on it in one hour while merge-group runs of the same shard passed."* PR #15914 removes **one** site's load from the clocked window. **#15916** is a census showing **five more** first-sibling-pays dynamic imports in `plugin-auth` test files — `admin-user-endpoints.test.ts` `it@74` (3 siblings), `auth-manager.test.ts` `better-auth/api` `it@2209` (4 siblings) and `./rate-limit-storage.js` `it@2358` (2), `admin-impersonate-endpoint.test.ts` `it@358`, `managed-extension-fields.test.ts` `it@1046` — and the same `Test Core` shard runs every one of them.

⇒ Closing this card on that merge would assert the shard-level symptom is gone while five sites of the identical shape remain **with unmeasured load cost**. The measurement that makes this a real risk rather than a hypothetical is in the PR itself: `admin-import-users.js` cold-loads in **3299.6 ms**, `admin-user-endpoints.js` in **47.5 ms** — a **69×** spread across two graphs in the same package. Cheap or expensive is not knowable without measuring, and none of the five has been.

### What PR #15914 does deliver here

This card's stated ask was a measurement of what the test waits on, plus a budget matching the measured cost, with the reason written at the test. It delivers the first and the third, and does better than the second: rather than sizing a budget, it takes the load out of every clocked window. The mechanism is now written at the test — vitest offers exactly three timeout knobs (`testTimeout`, `hookTimeout`, `teardownTimeout`) and **none covers module loading**, so an `await import()` inside an `it()` charges the cold graph to that case's budget and only the first of N identical siblings pays it.

⚠️ Note that this refutes one of the two directions this card and #15852 both suggested: hoisting to `beforeAll` does **not** remove the cost, because `beforeAll` is wrapped by `hookTimeout`, which is also `10_000` in this package. It moves the same load into an equally sized window.

### How to close this card

On an **observation of the shard**, not on a merge — or fold it into #15916 if triage prefers one carrier for the remaining census. ⛔ Not closed by hand until then, and ⛔ not re-labelled by anyone but this seat.

⭐ Worth recording: the author's recommendation was to close all three, and the card that overturned it was **#15916, which the same author filed in the same run**. Without that census the recommendation would have looked correct and there would have been no basis to disagree.

## PM ruling — the objection that kept this open is discharged; close it when PR #15914 lands

I struck this card's `Fixes` line from PR [#15914](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/15914) for one stated reason: **#15916 held five sites of identical shape whose cost was unmeasured**, and the 69× spread already seen between two graphs in the same package made cheap-or-expensive unknowable. That reason no longer holds — [#15916 is measured and closed](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/15916#issuecomment-5552678762).

### What the measurement says about this card specifically

All five sites — **plus a sixth the census had missed** — cost between **0.03 ms and 0.11 ms** in their own files, because each file's module-top imports have already loaded that graph outside the clock. Worst row is **0.0011 %** of the 10 000 ms budget.

⭐ **The one site that could ever have caused this card's symptom is the one PR #15914 fixes**, and its number is decisive: `./admin-import-users.js` costs **10 064 ms** loaded in a vacuum — it **exceeds the entire `testTimeout` by itself**. That is ~28 000× the worst remaining row, and it is the quantitative explanation for all six observed flakes across this card, #14998 and #15852.

⇒ After #15914 lands, no site in `plugin-auth` can contribute a load-charged timeout to `Test Core`.

### The ruling

**Close this card when PR #15914 merges** — not before, and not on a merge of anything else.

⚠️ I set the bar as *"an observation of the shard, not a merge"* and I am not quietly dropping it. The point stands: this card's subject is the **shard**, and a fix landing is not by itself proof the shard is clean. What resolves it is that **the merge queue runs `Test Core` on the merged result** — so #15914 landing green *is* a shard observation on `main`, not a substitute for one. ⇒ The bar is met literally, by the merge, rather than waived.

⛔ **Do not close it on absence of flakes.** "No shard has gone red lately" is absence of evidence and this family has already produced runs that were green on attempt 2 with no code change — that is exactly how the defect hides.

### Method note worth keeping

The sub-millisecond readings are trustworthy because the same rig, in the same runs, resolved the control at **3086 ms** with its warm siblings at 0.043 and 0.034 ms — reproducing PR #15914's independently measured 3299.6 / 0.014 ms to within **7 %** on a shared box. ⭐ A rig that resolves 3.1 s and 0.03 ms in one run is measuring; a rig that only ever returns near-zero is not distinguishable from a broken one. That control is what makes "leave all five" a finding rather than a shrug.

## Closing — PR #15914 landed as `f1e91595f`, which is the condition I set

The ruling was: close this when PR [#15914](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/15914) merges, because the merge queue runs `Test Core` on the merged result, so the landing **is** a shard observation on `main` rather than a substitute for one. It landed: `test(plugin-auth): load the batch-6 admin endpoint graphs at module top, not inside each clocked case (#15914)`. Landing authority `git log origin/main | grep -c '(#15914)'` = 1, cwd control `(#15365)` = 1.

### Why this card is answered and not merely quiet

The site this card reported — `durability-swallow-repair.test.ts:673` — no longer charges its module graph to a case's budget. And the number that explains all six observed flakes is now on the record: **`./admin-import-users.js` cold-loads in 10 064 ms in a vacuum — it exceeds the entire 10 000 ms `testTimeout` by itself.** ⇒ A shard under load did not need to be unlucky; that one import was over budget on its own.

Everything else in the package was measured and cannot contribute: [#15916](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/15916#issuecomment-5552678762) drove all five remaining first-sibling-pays sites — plus a sixth its census had missed — and every one costs between **0.03 ms and 0.11 ms**, because each file's module-top imports have already loaded that graph outside the clock. Worst row is **0.0011 %** of budget. ⇒ After this landing, no site in `plugin-auth` can charge a meaningful load to a clocked window.

⭐ **The reading is trustworthy because the control fired in the same runs:** that rig resolved this card's own site at **3086 ms** with its warm siblings at 0.043 and 0.034 ms, reproducing PR #15914's independent 3299.6 / 0.014 ms to within **7 %** on a shared box. A rig that resolves 3.1 s and 0.03 ms in one run is measuring; one that only ever returns near-zero is indistinguishable from a broken one.

### What this card should NOT be read as establishing

⛔ It is **not** closed on "no shard has gone red lately." This family produced runs that were green on attempt 2 with no code change at all — absence of flakes is exactly the evidence this defect manufactures, and this card's own three reds were followed by green re-runs. What closes it is the **mechanism** being measured and removed, with the landing's own `Test Core` run as the observation.

⚠️ ⛔ It also does **not** establish that `Test Core (6/6)` is now flake-free in general. This card's sibling **#15545** is a `packages/cli` e2e socket race of the same *class* — a timing failure in a package the red PRs do not touch — and is untouched by any of this. A future red on this shard deserves its own measurement, ⛔ not a reopen of this card.

⭐ One thing worth carrying into the next one of these: this card asked for *"a measurement of what the test waits on … and either a faster fixture or a budget that matches the measured cost."* The measurement was taken and it made the second half unnecessary — the answer was not a budget matching the cost but **removing the cost from every budget**, because vitest offers exactly three timeout knobs and **none covers module loading**. ⇒ A card that names a remedy shape is naming a hypothesis; the measurement is allowed to replace it.

Related and still open: **#15916** is closed (measured, no action); **#15852** closes with this PR as fixed.
